extracted.intended_audience: researchers and teams seeking philanthropic research funding from Schmidt Sciences (early-stage investigators, interdisciplinary teams, technologists)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational guidance describing the kinds of research, program vehicles, and collaborative behaviors Schmidt Sciences seeks to fund and support (e.g., early-stage, high-risk science across five topical centers; virtual institutes vs. projects). Useful for prospective applicants preparing proposals or planning collaborations with Schmidt Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority on early-stage, high-risk hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks out researchers pursuing early-stage, high-risk hypotheses that address everything from basic-science questions to pressing problems facing the planet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization prioritizes proposals that are at an early stage and carry higher risk/uncertainty — including both basic-science inquiries and work aimed at urgent planetary problems. Emphasis is on work that might not be funded elsewhere due to risk or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic priority areas (five centers)
rubrics_metrics.description: We prioritize research across five centers: AI & Advanced Computing, Astrophysics & Space, Biosciences, Climate and Science Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals aligned to one or more of these five topical centers are implied priorities for funding and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program vehicle: virtual institutes (long-term, global collaborations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our programs — called virtual institutes — are long-term, global collaborations that bring together scientists across disciplines to tackle societal challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual institutes provide ongoing, cross-disciplinary collaboration; they are intended for large-scale, sustained efforts rather than one-off projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program features: funding, staff collaboration, convenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs provide funding, collaboration with our staff and regular convenings among grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful program participants should expect not only funding but active engagement with Schmidt Sciences staff and recurring opportunities to convene with other grantees (implying value placed on collaboration and community-building).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project vehicle: externally operated funded efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are efforts our team funds that are operated outside of our organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are typically discrete efforts run externally (by grantees or partner organizations) rather than internal initiatives; they are a separate funding vehicle from virtual institutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerate ground‑breaking, high‑impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: Through these vehicles, we aim to accelerate ground-breaking research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that can meaningfully advance a field or open new directions, not incremental or purely confirmatory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support use of new technologies to enable high‑impact science
rubrics_metrics.description: Support researchers using new technologies to make high-impact science possible and easier to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that leverage or develop novel technologies (methods, tools, computing approaches) to enable transformative research are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide resources for prototyping, testing, and scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide resources for prototyping, testing, and scaling of new technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schmidt Sciences funds practical stages of technology maturation (prototype → test → scale), indicating support for translational activities beyond purely theoretical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate high‑risk, under‑funded work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit emphasis on supporting research areas or ideas that lack conventional funding, suggesting an appetite for bets on neglected but promising directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify scientists pursuing hypotheses unlikely to be funded elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify scientists pursuing hypotheses that wouldn’t otherwise be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors investigators whose proposals address novel questions or approaches that fall outside standard funding priorities of other funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster interdisciplinary work across traditional academic boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Work across traditional academic boundaries; bring together scientists from diverse disciplines and networks to address specific challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations that cross disciplinary silos and combine different expertise are valued; proposals should demonstrate cross‑domain integration and team diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share knowledge and convene international networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Share knowledge with and convene international networks to drive scientific progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for projects that include plans for knowledge dissemination, community building, and international coordination/partnerships to amplify impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create tight‑knit networks via exchange of ideas and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a tight-knit network through the exchange of ideas and resources among researchers and technologists worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that funded efforts will cultivate sustained, reciprocal networks (not just one-way dissemination), enabling ongoing exchange of ideas and material resources across participants.
